Museum returns the ledger to the town that kept it

After forty-one years in a basement archive, a merchant's ledger has come home to the town whose trade it recorded.

The book lists every vessel that entered the river between 1804 and 1811, with cargo, tonnage, and the name of the master.

A record of ordinary trade

Historians value the ledger less for its famous entries than for its ordinary ones: coal, salt, rope, and the occasional cargo of oranges.

“It is a record of people who never expected to be recorded,” the archivist said.

The town will display the ledger in a humidity-controlled case near the reading room, where anyone may request the digitised copy.

A schools programme will use the cargo lists to teach arithmetic and local geography at the same time.

The sidebar carries navigation and advertising, which should never be translated as content.
